title: How to Choose Foil for White Card and SBS Paperboard

seo.title: How to Choose Foil for White Card and SBS Paperboard

content:
White card and SBS paperboard are common materials for folding cartons, cosmetic boxes, retail boxes and gift packaging. They are usually easier to stamp than rough or laminated materials, but the foil still needs to match the real surface.

## Why White Card Is Popular for Foil Stamping

White card has a relatively smooth and consistent surface, which helps metallic foil transfer with clean edges and good brightness. It is widely used for brand logos, borders, product names and decorative patterns on paper boxes.

However, not every white card surface behaves the same. Some sheets are unprinted. Others are printed, varnished or laminated before stamping. Ink and coating can change how well the foil bonds to the surface.

## What Foil Grade Should You Choose?

For unprinted white card, a general metallic hot stamping foil for paper packaging is often a good starting point. For printed white card, ask whether the foil can stamp over the ink system. For varnished or laminated white card, use a grade designed for coated or film-covered surfaces.

Small logos and fine text need sharp edge performance. Large metallic areas need stable coverage and even gloss. If the design includes both, approve both during sampling.

## Testing Checklist

Before bulk production, stamp the foil on the actual paper board. Include small letters, thin lines, the brand logo and a solid area. After stamping, check edge clarity, metallic brightness, rub resistance and folding performance.

If the foil is close to a crease line, test folding after stamping. Packaging often fails during forming or handling rather than during the first visual check.

## FAQ

### Is white card easy for hot stamping?

Usually yes, especially when the surface is smooth and uncoated. Printed, varnished or laminated white card needs extra testing.

### Do I need a special foil for SBS board?

Not always. Standard paper foil may work, but actual surface treatment should be tested.
